key_insight: RecreationWorld shows that computer-use agents need to combine GUI interaction, coding, and visual verification in one loop rather than treating them as separate skills. It provides a scalable way to test whether agents can recreate a running reference environment from observation and action.
problem_solved: Most computer-use agents are evaluated either on graphical interface tasks or on code/software tasks, but real-world work requires both. This paper addresses the lack of a unified, verifiable benchmark for hybrid agents that must decide when to inspect, implement, and validate their outputs.
method: Introduces RecreationWorld, a five-platform benchmark framework centered on "recreation": agents observe a running reference and must reproduce it.
Evaluates hybrid CUAs that interleave GUI exploration, software implementation via code/CLI, and visual checking of results.
Emphasizes scalability and verifiability so agent behavior can be tested across multiple environments with clear outcome signals.
impact: For practitioners, this benchmark reflects more realistic digital work than isolated UI or coding tasks. It can help build and compare agents that are better at end-to-end automation, debugging, and environment-aware decision-making.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing observe → explore GUI → code/CLI → run → visually verify
Side-by-side comparison of graphical-only, code-only, and hybrid agents
Outcome/score chart showing recreation success and verification accuracy
paper_title: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents
paper_authors: Shuai Bai, Jiayong Deng, Yikun Fu, Chang Gao, Xuhao Hu
